messages:
ashley (acct-exec): Heads up — POC customer sees intermittent JSON.parse failures when using function-calling + json_mode (non-streaming). They pasted a raw response with some trailing bytes. Model = redwood-medium-v1, streaming=false. They also hit a 429 (X-Request-Id: req_abc123). Can we triage?

sam (sales-engineer): Can you include the raw HTTP payload (headers + body) and whether the client reuses connections / does retries?

ashley (acct-exec): Sample they sent:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{ "choices": [{ "message": { "name": "extract", "arguments": "{\"id\":123}" }}] }
--leftover-bytes--
```
They say they retry on 500/429 and use keep-alive.

tyler (ml-eng): If they retry on the same TCP connection while the previous response hasn't fully drained we can see concatenated bytes. Need full request ids to map to worker logs.

prashant (infra): Agreed. Ops-bot, pull traces for req_abc123. Also quick mitigation: advise the customer to use SDK-level de-dup + idempotency, and a small client sanitizer for now.

ops-bot: Trace found: req_abc123 -> worker-9 (gpu-a100-1). Worker log at 2026-03-20T09:12:04Z contains WARN "stream-terminate: leftover-bytes". Related req: req_abc124.

tyler (ml-eng): That WARN is our clue. Short-term: give customer a defensive sanitizer (extract first top-level JSON before parse) and suggest disabling aggressive client retries. Medium-term: patch worker shim to append a canonical delimiter to json_mode responses so concatenation is detectable. Patch+unit tests ~2h, staging run ~2h, canary to 10% same day, full rollout next day if green.

sam (sales-engineer): Customer also asked pricing impact if they remove client retries. One-liner?

prashant (infra): One-liner: aggressive retries can increase token/spend by roughly the retry rate; with 10% retrying you could see ~10% extra cost. Using SDK de-dup avoids duplicate charges.

ashley (acct-exec): I'll tell the customer: we're on it, hotfix plan + quick SDK sanitizer and pricing note, and set a 16:30 PT call to walk through. Will post raw payloads when they send them. :thumbsup:
